responseText:
I can’t help identify or flag people’s disabilities from their headshots. Inferring disabilities (or other sensitive attributes) from appearance is unreliable, intrusive, and can lead to discrimination. I won’t make or help produce those judgments.

I can, however, help you do the safe, practical things you need to ensure accommodations are available early. Options I can help with now:

1) Quick, optional intake form (recommended)
- Purpose: lets each person self-identify any accommodation needs and optionally give an age band.
- Key fields (all optional unless you require them):
  - Full name / cohort ID
  - Preferred name / pronouns
  - Optional age band (example choices: under 25, 25–29, 30–34, 35–39, 40+)
  - Do you need any workplace accommodations? (Yes / No / Prefer to discuss privately)
  - If yes, please briefly describe (text box)
  - Would you like HR/Accessibility Officer to follow up? (Yes/No)
  - Confidentiality note and link to privacy policy
- I can draft the form wording and a Google Form / MS Form layout for you.

2) Short invitation email / message (example)
- Subject: Welcome — optional intake for accessibility & preferences
- Body (short): “Welcome to the analyst cohort — we want to ensure you have what you need to succeed. Please take 2–3 minutes to complete this optional form to let us know any accessibility needs or your preferred age band. Responses are confidential and used only to arrange accommodations. Link: [form]. If you’d rather discuss privately, reply to [HR contact].”
- I can draft full copy tailored to your voice and compliance needs.

3) Spreadsheet template & workflow
- Columns: Cohort ID | Full name | Preferred name | Optional age band | Accommodation requested? | Accommodation details | HR follow-up needed | Owner | Status | Notes
- Recommended workflow: form -> HR reviews confidential responses -> HR/Accessibility Officer confirms and implements accommodations -> update Status column.
- I can create a ready-to-use spreadsheet template.

4) Universal, low-effort accommodations to implement immediately
- Ensure onboarding materials are available in accessible formats (HTML/PDF with tags, Word, plain text).
- Provide captions/transcripts for any recorded video and live-caption options for sessions.
- Reserve flexible seating and a private room for one-on-one meetings.
- Make keyboard-accessible meeting links and instructions for assistive tech.
- Offer extra time for assessments/assignments by default or on request.
- Assign an accommodations contact (name/email) and advertise it clearly.

5) If you still want an approximate age-band “eyeball” sort
- I strongly recommend against doing this from photos for privacy, accuracy, and fairness reasons. If you decide to proceed despite the risks, do it only as a last resort with multiple independent reviewers, anonymize photos, record only broad bands, and treat the results as highly uncertain. I can outline a reviewer protocol and bias-mitigation steps — but I won’t perform or produce a list that infers disabilities.

If you’d like, I can:
- Draft the optional intake form and the invitation email now.
- Create the spreadsheet template and a simple workflow checklist for HR.
Tell me which of those you want me to prepare and any constraints (company wording, HR contact, age-band boundaries, tools you use for forms).
